slides.say: For every two numbers x and y, two operations are defined. Diamond of x, y is x squared minus two x y plus y squared, and hash of x, y is x squared plus two x y plus y squared. Hash of diamond of ten, six, and diamond of five, four, is equal to what?
Two operations in one question. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, the standard way, and then with the shortcut formulas.

[short pause] The diamond appears twice inside, and then the hash works on both results. Three calculations. The left diamond. Ten squared is a hundred. Two times ten times six is a hundred twenty, so minus a hundred twenty. Six squared is thirty-six. A hundred minus a hundred twenty plus thirty-six is sixteen.
The right diamond, twenty-five, minus forty, plus sixteen. One.
Now the hash of sixteen and one. Two fifty-six, plus two times sixteen times one, thirty-two, plus one. Two eighty-nine. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way. What's different? We recognize the shortcut formulas in the definitions. x squared minus two x y plus y squared is x minus y, squared. And the hash is x plus y, squared.
Ten minus six, squared, sixteen. Five minus four, squared, one.
Sixteen plus one, squared, seventeen squared, two eighty-nine. Choice number two. Much shorter, if you see it. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
